interest: This document illustrates the State Department's cross-referencing and indexing practices within decimal file classifications covering currency reproduction and counterfeiting. It reveals how Japanese manufacturers appropriated U.S. currency imagery as decorative novelty motifs on consumer items like metal and leather cigarette cases during the interwar period. Additionally, it highlights American diplomatic surveillance of unauthorized foreign reproductions of U.S. dollar bills, even when produced as decorative novelties rather than circulating counterfeit tender.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5158, concerning counterfeiting and reproductions of obligations and securities in Japan. The lone entry records a January 22 despatch (No. 1647) from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reporting that Japanese manufacturers were producing metal and leather cigarette cases decorated with replicas of American dollar bills in various denominations. The sheet directs researchers to decimal file 811.5158/2111 for the full substantive document.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers sheet indexing a despatch from Ambassador Grew regarding the Japanese manufacture of cigarette cases decorated with replicas of American currency.
subfiles.summary: This List of Papers docket sheet records entry No. 1 under State Department decimal file 894.5158, categorized under counterfeiting and reproductions of obligations and securities in Japan. It purports despatch No. 1647 dated January 22 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, which reports that metal and leather cigarette cases featuring reproductions of U.S. dollar bills in various denominations were being manufactured in Japan. The entry includes a cross-reference notation directing researchers to file 811.5158/2111.
